morphology.look_here_first: Look at the ground-level rosette first: deeply lobed, lyre-shaped basal leaves form a flat rosette, with a relatively leafless flowering stalk rising above it.
diagnostic_traits: flowering stems rise well above rosette
small blue-lavender bilabiate flowers in spaced verticils
often in low moist/open woods, meadows, disturbed ground

confusers.separator: Both can form basal rosettes. Lyreleaf sage has the characteristic deeply lyre-shaped rosette and small blue-lavender flowers; cedar sage has broader cordate/lyrate leaves and red flowers in shaded juniper habitat.

installation_guardrail: Do not install until the range hold is resolved and Calvin approves.
